transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Once I start eating, especially at night after work, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely powerless over it, and it's really starting to worry me.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as forced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the use of laxatives?

I don't throw up or use laxatives, but I punish myself by only drinking coffee the entire next day and forcing myself to walk around the fairgrounds or mall parking lot for hours until my knees ache. This happens about once or twice a week to try to burn off the food. It's incredibly exhausting and I feel so ashamed of doing it.
Do you feel that these episodes of overeating are accompanied by a sense of losing control, and do you feel significant distress or shame specifically about the amount you consumed?

Yes, it absolutely feels like a switch flips and I go on autopilot, unable to stop even when I'm screaming at myself to do so. Afterward, I feel this intense shame and physical sickness from being so stuffed, and I just feel like a complete failure.
Do you feel that these compensatory actions, such as fasting or excessive exercise, are a way to prevent weight gain, or are they a way to soothe the intense guilt and shame you feel after eating?

It’s really a mix of both. It feels like a punishment because of the intense guilt, and I'll tell myself I don't deserve real food after failing so badly the night before. At the same time, I am so terrified of the scale going up even a single pound that I feel this desperate need to burn off all those calories.

When you engage in these periods of fasting or excessive exercise, is it driven more by a desire to prevent weight gain because of an intense fear of becoming fat, or is it primarily a form of self-punishment for the perceived loss of control?

It is really a combination of both. I feel a strong urge to punish myself, telling myself I don't deserve real food after losing control and forcing myself to walk until my knees ache. At the same time, I have this deep fear of gaining weight and looking big in my professional suits, and if the scale goes up even a pound, I feel like a complete failure.

When you engage in these compensatory behaviors like fasting or excessive exercise, do you feel they are an attempt to 'undo' the calories you consumed, or are they a rigid, regular part of your life even on days when you haven't binged?

They are definitely an attempt to 'undo' the overeating and punish myself. I only do things like drinking just coffee or walking for hours the day after an episode because I feel like I don't deserve real food. It isn't a regular routine on days when I've managed to eat normally.

When you engage in these compensatory behaviors, do you feel they are primarily a reaction to the specific binge episodes, or do you also feel a persistent, intense drive to maintain a very low body weight or thinness regardless of whether you have binged?

They are primarily a direct reaction to punish myself and 'make up for' the out-of-control eating from the night before. While I do worry constantly about my weight and how I look in my professional suits, the intense restriction and excessive walking are definitely triggered by the guilt of having binged.
Do you ever engage in self-induced vomiting or the misuse of laxatives, diuretics, or enemas to manage your weight after these episodes?

No, I have never made myself throw up, and I don't use laxatives, diuretics, or anything like that. Instead, my way of dealing with it is to punish myself by drinking only coffee the next day and forcing myself to walk laps around the fairgrounds or mall parking lot for hours until my knees ache. I just feel like I have to burn off the food to make up for what I did.
